topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the core learning objectives, and sets the clinical and biological perspective for studying cancer.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer: mutations, differentiation failure, and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises from accumulated genetic changes that disrupt normal cellular differentiation programs and tissue organization, and discuss the challenges of modeling this three-dimensional biology in vitro.

topics.label: Pathology, progression, classification, and clinical effects of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the distinctions between benign and malignant neoplasms, examining mechanisms of invasion and metastasis, stepwise histological progression, diagnostic nomenclature, and the pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence across humans and diverse animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze epidemiological patterns of cancer incidence and mortality in human populations alongside the prevalence of tumors across companion animals and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Clinical symptoms and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the initial presentation of cancer and evaluate the effectiveness, methods, and limitations of screening programs for detecting precursor and malignant lesions across different organs.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and giving housekeeping details for the practical sessions and upcoming lectures.
